chapters.title: The Window Seat
chapters.html:
On the morning train, I opened a notebook and drew a rectangle around the view. The frame did not change the landscape. It changed where I looked. A narrow canal passed a row of gardens, and every garden held a different answer to the same small question: what belongs here?

I wrote notice before naming at the top of the page. [1]

A useful question leaves room for an unexpected answer.

By the next station, I had stopped trying to capture everything. Three details were enough: a blue gate, a tilted chair, and a pear tree tied to the wall.

Notes

[1] This observation is an invitation to slow down, not a rule about taking notes.

chapters.title: Making a Small Shelf
chapters.html:
A shelf begins with the objects it will hold. I placed the cup, the clock, and the folded letter on the table before measuring any wood. Their arrangement told me more than an empty drawing could.

The first board was too deep. Instead of changing the room to fit it, I marked a new edge. A small test can save a large correction.

TrialDepth
First24 cm
Revised18 cm

The workshop timer used this tiny instruction:

for minute in range(3):
    pause()
    look_again()

At sunset the shelf held the same three objects. The useful change was the empty space around them.
